So if your organization owns a device with one Device CAL assigned to it, every user in your organisation can access the server software through that device. A single Device CAL is required for each client device (workstation, laptop, PDA, or smartphone) regardless of how many users access the server software from that device. Device CALs usually work best when there's one workstation per employee, and multiple people use each workstation over the course of a day.
RDS CALs: If you run Terminal Services (also known as Remote Desktop Services in Windows Server 2008) on a server, any user accessing the terminal services server requires a Remote Desktop Services (RDS) CAL in addition to any other Windows CALs they need.
As a rule of thumb, pick a type of CAL and stick with it, organisation-wide, for each product. This keeps your licensing simple and easy to manage. If you stick with one type of CAL and later realise that the other type would have suited you better, it's usually possible to switch the type of CALs you own, but this usually requires some paperwork and potentially some additional cost, depending on how you obtained your licenses.

Understanding how inflammation is fought... and why COX is still an issue
by Elizabeth Bland
Nothing gives your body a wakeup call like inflammation. It's your body's way of saying, "Hey, something is wrong, and I'm going to let you know."
The COX proteins kick-start inflammation. But they also make prostaglandins, which are lipid compounds that work within the body. Some prostaglandins actually serve to fight inflammation and pain, while others, well, serve to let your body know when it's damaged.
If you've ever used aspirin to fight a headache, you've harnessed the power of COX. Aspirin and other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) fight inflammation by inactivating the COX proteins. This fight, though, means the body also inactivates some prostaglandins, which actually do your body a world of good.
This is one reason for the fight that is going on in your body right now, and it is one reason why COX is still an issue. By inactivating COX, NSAIDs may cause some of the fight against inflammation and pain to become a fight against your body's good prostaglandins.

A fourth way of gaining knowledge, besides acquaintance with particular and universals, is inference. If I infer that all men are mortal from the premise that all known men are mortal, then I am inferring a general from a general. If I infer that all men are mortal from the observation that all men we know are mortal, then I am inferring a general from a particular. The most philosophically interesting inference, however, is from a particular to a particular and from a general to a particular. If I infer that Socrates is mortal from the premise that all men are mortal, I am still inferring, only this time through deduction. If I infer that Socrates is mortal because he is a man, then I am making an inference from a particular to a particular. Inferences from particulars to particulars may be justified in the same way that inference from particulars to universals are justified. Cori spezzati was developed in northern Italy in the early 1500s and reached its peak in the late 1500s and early 1600s. Giovanni Gabrieli (c.1554/1557-1612) used polychoral techniques at San Marco in Venice with great effect. Cori spezzati ultimately gave way to antiphonal psalmody of the Baroque era and to concertato pieces, especially the sacred concertos that were important in the early seventeenth century.
While the cori spezzati style is frequently associated with Venice and came to prominence there thanks to composers like Adrian Willaert (c. 1490-1562), the musical innovations in St Mark's Basilica, including spatially separated choirs, may have origins elsewhere in northern Italy.
